correctness.rationale: The two reduced Artin–Schreier classes (t², a t²+b t) are independent because c+a d is nonzero for every nonzero (c,d) over Fp, with break 2 at infinity. Different 3(p²−1) and Riemann–Hurwitz give genus g=(p²−1)/2; each of p+1 line quotient covers is w^p−w=At²+Bt, so over algebraically closed k is D_p:v²=u^p−u of genus h=(p−1)/2. Cross pullback–norm correspondences vanish through Jac(P¹), diagonal is [p], giving Φ^∨Φ=[p]_A and exact degΦ=p^g, with maximal isotropic kernel. Hyperelliptic Cartier–Manin residues p i−j avoid all monomial exponents h+(p−1)r, so each D_p Jacobian is superspecial; isogeny gives all slopes 1/2 for C. Ekedahl genus bound g≤p(p−1)/2 excludes superspeciality of C, also at p=3. Independently verified exact Cartier coefficient vanishing p=3,5,7,11,13; bounded checks are not proof for all p.
residual_risks: Kernel internal group scheme and complete Ekedahl–Oort type not determined; polarization identity is at finite-group-scheme level, not separable isogeny.
